title: Temple and Puja Outfits for Women Abroad: Modest, Comfortable Looks
excerpt: Temple and puja outfits for women abroad: modest, comfortable and traditional kurta sets, plus tips on colours, dupattas, footwear and cold weather.
body:
The best outfit for a temple or puja is modest, comfortable to sit in and easy to cover your head with. A cotton kurta set with a dupatta is the simplest choice, because it covers shoulders and knees, lets you sit cross-legged on the floor and works in every season with a few layers. Here is how to dress with ease and respect, wherever you live.

## What temples usually expect

Dress codes vary from temple to temple and between communities, so it is always worth checking the temple's website or asking someone who visits regularly. Most share a few common expectations:

- Shoulders, upper arms and knees covered
- Loose, non-transparent clothing
- A dupatta or scarf available to cover the head where it is customary, such as in a gurdwara
- Shoes removed before entering, sometimes socks too
- Leather items, such as belts and bags, kept to a minimum in some temples

Abroad, temples are often community centres as well as places of worship. You may sit for a long havan, help in the kitchen or stay for a langar or prasad meal, so practical clothing matters as much as tradition.

## The easiest outfits for temple and puja

| Outfit | Why it works | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Straight kurta, pants and dupatta | Fully covered, easy to sit in, dupatta for the head | Regular visits, havan, gurdwara |
| Anarkali with churidar | Traditional, graceful, plenty of room when seated | Festivals, family pujas |
| Kurta with palazzos | Very comfortable on the floor | Long ceremonies, seva |
| Long tunic with trousers | Simple and quick | Weekday visits after work |

A light set like the [Navy Blue Kota Doria Embroidered Kurta Pant Dupatta Set](/products/navy-blue-kota-doria-embroidered-kurta-pant-dupatta-set/) is ideal. Kota doria is airy, the dupatta is easy to drape over the head, and navy looks dignified for any occasion.

## Choosing colours for puja

Bright, auspicious colours are traditionally loved at pujas: yellow, red, orange, green, pink and saffron tones. Yellow is a favourite for Saraswati puja and Basant Panchami, and red and maroon are popular for festive pujas. Many families avoid all-black outfits for auspicious ceremonies, and white is worn in some traditions and avoided in others, so follow your family's custom.

For a cheerful everyday temple look, the [Yellow Embroidered Cotton Tunic Top](/products/yellow-black-embroidered-cotton-tunic-top/) with straight white trousers and a light scarf works well.

For a festival puja around Diwali on 8 November, a richer shade such as the [Plum Purple Embroidered Cotton Suit Set](/products/plum-purple-embroidered-cotton-3-piece-suit/) feels special but stays modest.

## Fabric and comfort

Cotton is the best fabric for temple wear. It breathes when you sit close to a havan fire, it does not cling when you bow, and it washes easily if a little ghee or kumkum lands on it. Hand block printed cotton feels especially fitting for a sacred space because it is made slowly, by hand. Explore our [hand block print](/hand-block-print-kurta-sets/) collection if you like that handmade feel.

Avoid very fitted kurtas or stiff fabrics. You should be able to sit cross-legged, kneel and stand up again without adjusting your clothes. Pants with a drawstring or elastic waist are far more comfortable on the floor than tight leggings.

## Dressing for cold weather

Temples in the UK, Canada and the northern USA can be chilly, and you will often remove your shoes at the door. A few smart layers help:

- A thin thermal under your kurta
- A soft wool shawl over the dupatta, which can also cover the head
- Warm socks, if the temple allows them, or carry a pair in your bag
- A long coat that comes off easily at the entrance

The [Mint Green Hand Block Print Cotton Kurta Pant Dupatta Set](/products/mint-green-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-dupatta-set-with-hand-work-yoke/) layers neatly over a thermal and under a shawl.

## Small details that make a difference

- **Dupatta:** Choose one that is long and soft enough to stay on your head without constant adjusting.
- **Footwear:** Slip-on flats or juttis that are easy to remove and put back on.
- **Jewellery:** Keep it simple. A pair of earrings and a few bangles are plenty.
- **Bag:** A small cloth bag for your phone, keys and a donation envelope.
- **Hair:** Tie long hair back, especially if you will be near a diya or havan fire.

Temple wear should never feel tight when you sit. We stitch to your bust, waist, hip and height at no extra cost, and you can ask for a slightly relaxed fit for long ceremonies.

## Frequently asked questions

**Can I wear jeans to a temple abroad?**
Many temples accept neat trousers or jeans with a long tunic, but a kurta set is more traditional and more comfortable for sitting on the floor.

**Do I need to cover my head at a temple?**
It depends on the place. It is expected in gurdwaras and customary in some temples. Carrying a dupatta or scarf means you are always prepared.

**What colours are best for a puja?**
Yellow, red, orange, green and pink are traditional favourites. Check your family's customs about black and white.

**What fabric is most comfortable for long pujas?**
Cotton and kota doria are light, breathable and easy to sit in for hours.
